newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SUGAR BEET OUTPUT SEEN SLUMPING.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SUGAR BEET OUTPUT SEEN SLUMPING.

text.p: Bulgaria's Sugar Institute said on Friday it expects processed sugar beet output to fall to 66,000 tonnes of this year from 147,040 tonnes of sugar beet last year, due to bad weather and scarse funds.
"The estimated sugar beet yield will be catastrofically low because of bad weather conditions and lack of funds," Sugar Institute director Botyo Mitev told Reuters.
Mitev said he expected this year's white sugar output also to fall to 7,100 tonnes or half of last year's 14,715 tonnes.
The beet area this year was reduced to 6,000 ha from 11,200 ha last year, he said.
Local farmers had difficulties obtaining funds due to the general economic crisis in the country.
Only two of the seven sugar-processing plants are operating now due to lack of raw material, said Mitev.

Bulgaria, which used to meet nearly 50 percent of its SUGAR needs from local production, now supplies its sugar-processing plants with less than 10 percent of their requirements. -- Jana Katsarova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
